tasks.title: cairn init: add missing entries to an existing .cairn/.gitignore
tasks.description:
Today `initCoreFiles()` (src/commands/init.ts:91) writes `GITIGNORE_CONTENT` only when `.cairn/.gitignore` does not exist, so every project initialized before round 15 is missing the run-state, prompt-file, test-log and hook-error entries (`.cairn_run_state.json`, `.cairn_run_state.json.lock`, `.cairn_task_*_prompt.md`, `.cairn_task_*_tests.log`, `.cairn_hook_errors.log`) and an agent's `git add -A` can commit those files.

Add an append-only merge for the existing-file case: compare the existing file's lines (trimmed, exact string match, WHEREVER in the file they appear — position independent) against the lines of `GITIGNORE_CONTENT`, and append only the missing non-comment lines under a short comment header. Never reorder, rewrite or remove an existing line — the legacy `.ralph_*` block and any user additions must survive byte-for-byte. Print `  Updated: <dirName>/.gitignore (added N entries)` when N > 0 and print nothing when nothing was added. `init` must still never touch the repository's root `.gitignore`.

Tests (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): an old-style file containing only the legacy `.ralph_*` block gains the missing current entries; a file that already contains all the entries MID-FILE (not at the end) is left unchanged with no output; user-added lines are preserved; a second `init` adds nothing — the existing re-init test at test/commands/init.test.ts:170 must still pass.

NEVER run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, `cairn init`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init …` against this repository's root, and never spawn a real post-task reviewer against this repo. Exercise these code paths only in temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync`.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT modify `package.json`'s `build` script — the binary is pinned for this round and the health check is redirected to /tmp/cairn-healthcheck. Do NOT run `./install.sh`. `cairn.json` has an uncommitted user change: stage only the files you changed.
tasks.notes:
# Task #117 — cairn init: add missing entries to an existing .cairn/.gitignore

## What changed

`src/commands/init.ts`:
- Added `currentGitignoreEntries()` — returns `GITIGNORE_CONTENT`'s non-comment,
  non-blank lines, trimmed.
- Added `mergeGitignoreEntries(gitignorePath)` (exported) — append-only merge:
  reads the existing file, builds a `Set` of its trimmed non-blank lines
  (position-independent), diffs against `currentGitignoreEntries()`, and
  appends only the missing ones under a new `# Added by cairn init (missing
  entries)` header. Returns the count appended (0 if nothing missing). Never
  rewrites, reorders, or removes existing lines; if nothing is missing the
  file is not touched at all (not even a trailing-newline normalization).
- `initCoreFiles()`'s existing-`.gitignore` branch now calls
  `mergeGitignoreEntries()` instead of doing nothing, and prints
  `  Updated: <dirName>/.gitignore (added N entries)` when N > 0, nothing when
  N is 0. The fresh-file branch (`fs.writeFileSync(gitignorePath,
  GITIGNORE_CONTENT)`) is unchanged, so a brand-new project still gets a
  `Created:` message and root `.gitignore` is still never touched (only
  `dataDir/.gitignore` is read/written).

`test/commands/init.test.ts`:
- Rewrote the old "does not overwrite existing .gitignore" test (it asserted
  byte-for-byte equality with a bare `# custom\n` file, which is exactly the
  behavior this task changes) into "does not overwrite existing .gitignore,
  but appends missing entries" — content still starts with the original text,
  gains the new entries, and prints the `Updated: ... (added N entries)` line.
- Added the four TDD tests the task asked for:
  - old-style file with only the legacy `.ralph_*` block (using the pre-round
    GITIGNORE_CONTENT format: `.ralph_complete`, `.ralph_iterations.log`,
    etc.) gains the 12 missing `.cairn_*` entries, original content preserved
    byte-for-byte, prints "added 12 entries".
  - a file that already has every current entry, in different order and
    mid-file (a trailing user comment + `node_modules/` follow), is left
    byte-for-byte unchanged with no `.gitignore`-related stdout line.
  - user-added lines (`my-scratch-dir/`, `*.local`) survive a merge that adds
    the missing cairn entries.
  - a second `initCoreFiles()` call on an already-merged file changes nothing
    and prints nothing.
  - explicit test that init never touches the project root's `.gitignore`.
- Confirmed the existing idempotency test at (now) test/commands/init.test.ts
  around line 170 ("is idempotent — running twice produces same files") still
  passes unmodified: a freshly-created `.gitignore` already contains every
  `GITIGNORE_CONTENT` line, so the second run's merge is a no-op.

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/init.test.ts` — 179 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run typecheck` — clean.
- `bun test` (full suite) — 1200 pass, 0 fail.
- All exploration/build/test work was local TS edits and `bun test`/`bun run
  typecheck` only. No `cairn round`, `cairn hook`, `cairn init`, or
  `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init` was run against this repo's root, and no
  real post-task reviewer was spawned. Did not touch `cairn.json`'s
  `healthCheck`, `package.json`'s `build` script, or run `./install.sh`.

## Follow-ups / discovered issues

None found unrelated to this task.

tasks.title: Hook: deny $ anywhere in reviewer Bash; fold Writer into cli-io.ts
tasks.description:
Confirmed hole (probed during planning): `hasOutputOption()` (src/commands/hook.ts) strips `'`, `"`, `\` and `$` from each token but leaves braces, so `git log --output${X}=/tmp/f` becomes `--output{X}=/tmp/f`, matches neither `--output` nor `--output=`, is ALLOWED, and bash then expands `${X}` to nothing and git writes the file. The pre-check regex at hook.ts:105 (/[`<>]|\$\(/) only catches backticks, `<`, `>` and `$(`.

Fix: in `isInspectionOnly()`, deny any reviewer Bash command containing `$` ANYWHERE, replacing the strip-`$`-then-check approach; this subsumes `$(`, `${…}`, `$VAR` and `$'…'` ANSI-C quoting. Keep the exact-token `--output` / `--output=` check as a second layer (stop stripping `$` in `hasOutputOption` since `$` is now denied outright). This is safe for legitimate use: the `${range}` in src/post-task-reviewer.ts's prompt is a JS template literal filled in before the reviewer ever sees it, so the reviewer's git commands never contain a literal `$`. Update the deny reason text to mention shell variables/expansion alongside redirection, command substitution and `--output`.

Also fold hook.ts:30's local `Writer` type declaration into an import from src/cli-io.ts (the other copies moved there in #115).

Tests (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): newly denied — `git log --output${X}=/tmp/f`, `git diff $X`, `git show $'--output=x'`; still allowed — a plain `git diff <sha>..<sha>` range, `git log --oneline -5`, `git status`; still denied — the existing quoting variants (`--output"="…`, `--outpu't'=…`, `--output\=…`) and redirection.

tasks.title: Hook: find the project from the tool call's cwd, not CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT
tasks.description:
`findProjectRoot()` (src/utils.ts:68) checks `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` first, and the hook calls it with the tool call's `cwd` (hook.ts:187), so the environment variable wins. A /cairn-run session started from a shell cairn launched therefore resolves the hook's `tasksFilePath` and `reviewsDir` to the wrong project — observed during planning, where a hook aimed at a temp repo resolved to this repo instead.

Fix: when the PreToolUse payload has a usable string `cwd`, the hook resolves the project by walking up from that `cwd` for a `.cairn/` directory, IGNORING `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`; with no usable `cwd`, fall back to today's behavior (env var, then `process.cwd()`). The same resolution must be used for the fail-open error-log location (hook.ts:209), so a deny and its error log never point at different projects. Suggested shape: an options argument on `findProjectRoot` (e.g. `{ ignoreEnv: true }`) or a small walk-only helper exported from src/utils.ts.

DO NOT change `findProjectRoot`'s default behavior — every other cairn command relies on the env var winning, and changing it would break commands spawned by cairn.

Test (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): with `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` set to temp project A and the payload's `cwd` inside temp project B, the reviewer's `reviews/` scope and the `tasks.json` deny rule both resolve to B; with no `cwd` in the payload, A still wins. Save and restore `process.env.CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` around the tests.

NEVER run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, `cairn init`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init …` against this repository's root, and never spawn a real post-task reviewer against this repo. Exercise these code paths only in temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync`.

tasks.title: Headless reviewer: --disallowedTools closes the same --output hole
tasks.description:
`cairn run`'s headless reviewer is contained only by `--allowedTools` prefix rules (`Bash(git diff:*)` etc.), which cannot exclude an argument — so it can still run `git diff --output=<file>` (CLAUDE.md calls this the "remaining headless gap").

A probe run during planning CONFIRMED both the hole and the fix: with `--allowedTools "Bash(git log:*)"` and no deny, `git log --output=/tmp/f` ran and wrote the file; adding `Bash(*--output*)` blocked both the plain form and the `--output${X}=` variable form; adding `Bash(*$*)` plus the quote patterns also blocked the split-quoting form `git log --out"put"=/tmp/f`. `git log --oneline -3` still ran (no false positives).

Add a `--disallowedTools` argument to the reviewer spawn in `spawnPostTaskReviewer` (src/post-task-reviewer.ts) carrying that validated list — `Bash(*--output*)`, `Bash(*--out*)`, `Bash(*$*)` and the quote patterns (`Bash(*")` and the single-quote equivalent) — and define the list as an exported constant BESIDE `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` in src/claude-settings.ts, so the headless deny rules and the hook's parsed checks stay visibly paired even though they can't be made identical.

Watch the pattern syntax: the probe found `Bash(git log:* --output*)` matches nothing (the `:` prefix form does not combine with a trailing wildcard), so use the forms listed above verbatim.

Test (TDD — write the failing test first, watch it fail, then make it pass): assert the spawn is invoked with `--disallowedTools` followed by the expected value — use the existing injected `spawn` dependency. NEVER spawn a real reviewer against this repo, and do not try to re-probe Claude Code's matching behavior from a unit test.

Known and accepted limit, to document rather than solve: deny patterns match raw command text while the hook parses the command, so /cairn-run remains the stronger layer — this is defense in depth against a trusted agent, not a sandbox.

NEVER run `cairn round …`, `cairn hook …`, `cairn init`, or `bun src/index.ts round|hook|init …` against this repository's root. Exercise these code paths only in temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync`.
